finalText: Overfitting occurs when a machine learning model learns the training data too thoroughly, capturing not only the underlying patterns but also the random noise and fluctuations specific to that dataset. As a result, the model performs exceptionally well on the training examples yet fails to generalize to new, unseen data, producing poor predictive performance when deployed in practice. Mitigation strategies include regularization techniques, cross-validation, early stopping during training, and simplifying the model architecture to better balance bias and variance.
